Laukzeme Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klaipėdos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Laukžeme's Jewish community, established in the second half of the 17th century with just 23 members, largely relocated to nearby Darbėnai sometime during the 18th century — reportedly after a local nobleman, angered by a miscommunication, expelled them from his property — though those who stayed continued trading with Liepāja and Riga; by 1784, only two Jewish families remained. Despite the community's move, burials continued in this cemetery into the 19th century, and even sporadically as late as 1913. Only one legible tombstone survives today, marking the grave of Yenta Katz, a rabbi's daughter buried between 1819 and 1828; the site was recognized as a historical monument in 2005 and features in a regional travel guide to the Kretinga area.
